module.title: Pricing
module.description: Sales prices of articles: proposing them, approving them and expiring them. It makes sure a sales price is never below the purchase price. Discounts per customer are out of scope (see DEC-001).

userStory.raw: As a pricing analyst (PER-PRICING-ANALYST), I want to propose a sales price for an article, so that it can be sold at a price that covers what we pay.
userStory.goal: propose a sales price for an article
userStory.benefit: it can be sold at a price that covers what we pay

sections.Summary and user story: As a pricing analyst (PER-PRICING-ANALYST), I want to propose a sales price for an article, so that it can be sold at a price that covers what we pay.
sections.Business value / problem: New articles and changed purchase prices get a sales price quickly, and never one below the purchase price.
sections.Preconditions and triggers: An article was activated (EVT-ARTICLE-ACTIVATED) or one of its purchase prices changed (EVT-PURCHASE-PRICE-CHANGED). The article appears on SCR-PRC-01 as waiting for a sales price.
sections.Main flow:
1. On SCR-PRC-01, the pricing manager opens an article waiting for a sales price.
2. They see its valid purchase prices and its current sales price, if any.
3. They use action A01 Propose and enter the amount and the valid-from date.
4. The amount is checked against the highest valid purchase price (RULE-PRC-001).
5. The sales price is saved as proposed and waits for approval.
sections.Alternative and exception flows:
- The amount is not higher than the highest valid purchase price: nothing is saved and the pricing manager sees the purchase price (RULE-PRC-001).
- The article is no longer active: nothing is saved (RULE-001).
- A proposed sales price already exists for the article: it is replaced by the new proposal.
sections.Data in / data out: In: article, amount, valid-from date. Shown: valid purchase prices, current sales price. Out: a proposed sales price.
sections.Business rules applied:
- RULE-001 — only active articles get a sales price.
- RULE-PRC-001 — the amount must be higher than the highest valid purchase price.
sections.State transitions caused: None. A new sales price starts as proposed.
sections.Notifications: None. The proposal appears on SCR-PRC-01 for approval.
sections.Permissions and data visibility: Pricing managers propose sales prices for all articles. Sales staff never see proposed prices.
sections.Acceptance criteria:
### CAP-PRC-001-AC-01

- **Given** an active article whose highest valid purchase price is 8.00
- **When** the pricing manager proposes a sales price of 10.00
- **Then** the sales price is saved as proposed
- **Covers:** main flow step 5

### CAP-PRC-001-AC-02

- **Given** an active article whose highest valid purchase price is 8.00
- **When** the pricing manager proposes a sales price of 7.50
- **Then** nothing is saved and the pricing manager sees the purchase price of 8.00
- **Covers:** RULE-PRC-001

### CAP-PRC-001-AC-03

- **Given** a discontinued article
- **When** the pricing manager proposes a sales price
- **Then** nothing is saved
- **Covers:** RULE-001
sections.Out of scope:
- Prices per customer group (DEC-001).
- Promotions and temporary discounts.

userStory.raw: As a pricing analyst (PER-PRICING-ANALYST), I want to approve a proposed sales price, so that sales staff use it from its valid-from date.
userStory.benefit: sales staff use it from its valid-from date

sections.Summary and user story: As a pricing analyst (PER-PRICING-ANALYST), I want to approve a proposed sales price, so that sales staff use it from its valid-from date.
sections.Business value / problem: No sales price reaches sales staff without a second look.
sections.Main flow:
1. On SCR-PRC-01, the pricing manager opens a proposed sales price.
2. They use action A02 Approve.
3. The proposal is checked again against the purchase price (RULE-PRC-001).
4. It becomes valid; the previous valid sales price of the article expires.
sections.Alternative and exception flows:
- A purchase price changed since the proposal and the amount no longer covers it: the approval is refused (RULE-PRC-001).
- The margin over the highest valid purchase price is below 10 percent: the approval is refused and the margin is shown (RULE-PRC-002).
sections.Data in / data out: In: the proposed sales price. Out: the valid sales price, the expired previous one.
sections.Business rules applied:
- RULE-001 — the article must still be active.
- RULE-PRC-001 — checked again at approval, because purchase prices may have changed.
- RULE-PRC-002 — the margin is checked at approval.
sections.State transitions caused: ENT-SALES-PRICE proposed -> valid; the previous one valid -> expired.
sections.Notifications: None. Sales staff see the new price from its valid-from date.
sections.Permissions and data visibility: Pricing managers approve sales prices for all articles.
sections.Acceptance criteria:
### CAP-PRC-002-AC-01

- **Given** a proposed sales price of 10.00 and a valid one of 9.00 for the same article
- **When** the pricing manager approves the proposal
- **Then** the price of 10.00 is valid
- **And** the price of 9.00 is expired
- **Covers:** main flow step 4

### CAP-PRC-002-AC-02

- **Given** a proposed sales price of 10.00 and a purchase price that rose to 10.50 since
- **When** the pricing manager approves the proposal
- **Then** the approval is refused and the new purchase price is shown
- **Covers:** RULE-PRC-001

### CAP-PRC-002-AC-03

- **Given** a proposed sales price of 10.50 and a highest valid purchase price of 10.00
- **When** the pricing manager approves the proposal
- **Then** the approval is refused and the margin of 5 percent is shown
- **Covers:** RULE-PRC-002
sections.Out of scope: - Approval by a second person (see open questions).
sections.Open questions: - Must the approver be a different person from the one who proposed the price?

capabilities.title: Expire sales prices of a discontinued article

userStory.raw: As a pricing analyst (PER-PRICING-ANALYST), I want the sales prices of a discontinued article to expire, so that nobody quotes them.
userStory.goal: the sales prices of a discontinued article to expire

sections.Summary and user story: As a pricing analyst (PER-PRICING-ANALYST), I want the sales prices of a discontinued article to expire, so that nobody quotes them.
sections.Business value / problem: Discontinued articles disappear from price lookups the same day.
sections.Main flow:
1. The article appears on SCR-PRC-01 with its valid and proposed sales prices.
2. The pricing manager uses action A03 Expire.
3. Its valid sales price expires and proposed ones are withdrawn.
sections.Alternative and exception flows: - The article has no valid sales price: it is removed from the list without changes.
sections.Data in / data out: In: the discontinued article. Out: expired sales prices.
sections.Business rules applied: - RULE-001 — a discontinued article has no valid sales price.
sections.Permissions and data visibility: Pricing managers expire sales prices for all articles.
sections.Acceptance criteria:
### CAP-PRC-003-AC-01

- **Given** a discontinued article with a valid sales price
- **When** the pricing manager expires its prices
- **Then** the sales price is expired
- **And** sales staff no longer see the article
- **Covers:** RULE-001

mainFlow: The article appears on SCR-PRC-01 with its valid and proposed sales prices.
The pricing manager uses action A03 Expire.
Its valid sales price expires and proposed ones are withdrawn.
exceptions: The article has no valid sales price: it is removed from the list without changes.

given: a discontinued article with a valid sales price
when: the pricing manager expires its prices
and: sales staff no longer see the article

personas.title: Pricing analyst
personas.description:
**Goals:** sales prices that cover the purchase price and are approved before anyone uses them.

**Pain points:** learns about purchase price increases weeks later.

entities.title: Article
entities.description: Something the company sells. Sales staff only ever see active articles.

attributes.name: Unit of measure
attributes.description: The unit it is sold in

entities.title: Purchase price
entities.description: What a supplier charges for one unit of measure of an article, from a given date.

entities.title: Sales price
entities.description: What the company charges for one unit of measure of an article, from a given date.

rules.title: Only active articles are sold
rules.statement: An article can have a valid sales price, and be shown to sales staff, only while it is active.

rules.title: Sales price covers the purchase price
rules.statement: A sales price must be higher than the highest valid purchase price of the same article.

rules.title: Sales prices keep a minimum margin
rules.statement: A sales price must be at least 10 percent higher than the highest valid purchase price of the same article.

events.title: Article activated
events.description: An article became active. Pricing is told so a sales price can be proposed.

events.title: Article discontinued
events.description: An article will no longer be sold. Its valid sales prices must expire.

events.title: Purchase price changed
events.description: A new purchase price became valid. Pricing checks whether the sales price still covers it.

screens.title: Sales price review
screens.purpose: Work through articles that need a sales price, proposals that need approval, and discontinued articles whose prices must expire.
